title: Thai JIC Presents Evidence Alleging Cambodian Military Use of Preah Vihear, Urges Independent Probe
detail: Air Chief Marshal Praphas Sonchaidee, director of the Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation, presented aerial photographs, coordinates and images of weapons -- including anti-tank RPGs, small arms and anti-aircraft positions -- that Thailand says show Cambodian forces used the Preah Vihear World Heritage site as a military position and fired from the area at Thai forces. Praphas called for independent verification of the evidence, cited the 1954 Hague Convention on cultural property protection, and said establishing a full timeline of deployment and weapons use was needed before assigning responsibility for damage to the temple. The statement follows Cambodia's September 9 UNESCO-ICOMOS report and September 10 CMAC assessment documenting extensive war damage at the site, which Cambodia attributes to deliberate Thai targeting.

title: Concrete Border Wall Rises in Pong Nam Ron, Chanthaburi
detail: Thai military engineers have completed roughly 1km of a planned 8.4km reinforced-concrete wall in Pong Nam Ron district, Chanthaburi province, near the Ban Pakkat crossing into Cambodia's Pailin province. The 3.6-metre barrier combines reinforced concrete panels with galvanized steel mesh and barbed wire. Royal Thai Army officer Captain Prachya Hantiem said the wall is meant to curb smuggling of people and goods, while local officials say it also cuts through farmland long used for informal cross-border movement. Village chief Itchira Aranchaiyasiri said residents welcome the added security even as historical cross-border access patterns are disrupted.
